prize_parts.citation: For the rational design of zeolite and molecular-sieve catalysts, in which pore architecture and active sites are controlled to direct catalytic function.

statement.case_for: I have reread the whole first round and my preferred configuration is unchanged: B018 with Corma, Davis and Zones. The case is scientific, not a count. Zeolite and molecular-sieve design is the clearest example on the shortlist of architecture determining function, and the structural evidence behind it is exceptional, because frameworks and the placement of sites within them have been determined and refined by diffraction for decades. Structure-directing agents and template chemistry (Zones, Davis) give synthetic control over topology, and Corma's work ties framework and active-site design to catalytic selectivity. The consequences are lasting and independently confirmed in cracking, hydrocracking, methanol-to-hydrocarbons, NOx abatement and fine-chemical catalysis. Chemistry has recognised catalysis and materials architecture before, but never this area. The chair's question about which kind of prize this year should be is not answered by round 1, and a materials-and-catalysis prize is a genuine alternative to the chemical-biology and methods candidates. I take the chair's point that two single-member positions need to show what would make them competitive. For B018 that would be a citation that names one achievement, design of catalysts by controlling pore architecture and site placement, rather than the whole history of zeolite synthesis.
statement.case_against: Round 1 did not move anyone toward B018. I remain its only supporter, so on the evidence of this exchange it has no route to five votes, and I do not treat my own field expertise as a substitute for that. The field is old and diffuse. Barrer, Milton and Breck laid the foundations and are outside any three-name set, Yu and Tsapatsis made major contributions that the three-name limit excludes, and Somfai's summary of my case as broad industrial reach is fair but also shows the risk that colleagues read it as incremental refinement of a long-established subject. I also have to allow that my closeness to the field inflates how clear the single achievement looks to me.

responses.point: Brzezinski keeps targeted protein degradation (B012) with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, arguing that the PROTAC concept and the cereblon mechanism together give a coherent, attributable story within three names, and accepts that choosing Handa over Ciulli leaves a structural contribution unrecognised.
responses.response: I do not think the story is as coherent as the citation suggests. Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target is a mechanistic discovery about molecular glues, whereas Crews and Deshaies conceived bifunctional PROTACs, and the clinical PROTACs use several E3 ligases, not only cereblon. A single sentence that covers both strands will have to be vague about the mechanism. By your own account Ciulli's VHL ligands and the ternary-complex structures are what turned PROTACs from a concept into design, and as a structural chemist I value exactly that evidence of how induced proximity works at atomic resolution. If B012 goes forward, I would prefer Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli with a citation confined to PROTAC design, and leave the glue lineage out. The absence of an approved degrader does not decide this for me, but it does mean the claim of changed practice rests on promise.

responses.point: Linke, answering the chair's own question, argues that base editing (B060) is a clear chemical principle that is easy to state in one sentence and separates the 2016-2017 discovery from later refinements such as prime editing, and he proposes the Liu, Komor and Gaudelli trio.
responses.response: The one-sentence principle is persuasive and the citation separates the discovery from later refinements, which I accept. I still disagree with the trio, and your statement and Chabes's both concede that Kondo and Nishida reported Target-AID essentially in parallel. That is a real attribution cost, not a footnote. I would rather credit Liu alone, or Liu with Komor and Gaudelli only if the citation is written around the two editors they built, and then say openly that the cytidine-deaminase fusion was reached independently elsewhere. On CRISPR-Cas9, I accept the argument that the 2020 prize recognised the nuclease and that deaminase engineering is new chemistry. The adenine editor is the strongest evidence, because an enzyme with no natural DNA substrate had to be evolved. I rank B060 as my second alternative on that basis.

responses.point: Aqvist keeps Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B055) with Buchwald and Hartwig, arguing that it is simple, general and has more than 25 years of independent confirmation, with a clean two-name attribution and no maturity question.
responses.response: The attribution and maturity are the cleanest on the list, and I said in round 1 that I would accept B055 as a sound option. My difference is on the chair's question of what it added beyond 2010. Your answer that ligand control of oxidative addition and reductive elimination made it general is a real advance, but it still operates within the Pd(0)/Pd(II) manifold already recognised, whereas zeolite design opens a separate architecture-to-function area. I would also place Kosugi's tin-amide work on the record: whether it anticipated the catalytic cycle is a point you and Somfai both say you are recalling from memory, and it needs checking in the expert material before the committee relies on a two-name configuration.

responses.point: Aili argues that induced proximity is a transferable design principle that moves pharmacology from occupancy to event-driven action, that degraders are already a research reagent class and a large clinical pipeline, and that B019 is the safer fallback if settled clinical impact is required.
responses.response: I agree that induced proximity is transferable and that degraders are already useful as reagents, and I take that as the strongest reply to the maturity objection. Where I disagree is that your citation joins two lineages that arose separately and that Handa's cereblon discovery explains the glue branch but not PROTACs built on VHL. I also note that your own case_against accepts that much of the novelty is medicinal-chemistry design. That is why I weigh the structural evidence of ternary complexes more than clinical pipeline size. I would not choose B019 over B012, since delivery lipids are a formulation success with a different attribution problem across many names.

uncertainties: Whether any colleague will move to B018 after round 1, and if none does, whether I should treat it as a position the committee will not reach.
Whether the PROTAC and molecular-glue strands of B012 can be stated as one achievement, and whether Ciulli's structural contribution should displace Handa.
Whether Kondo and Nishida (Target-AID) must be credited in B060, or whether a Liu-only or Liu, Komor and Gaudelli citation is defensible.
Whether Kosugi's precursor work to B055 is as limited as two members recall from memory.
Whether early zeolite pioneers outside the credited list create an attribution problem for B018 that the three-name limit cannot resolve.
statement.conflict_note: Unchanged from round 1. B018 lies in my own research field (zeolites and porous framework materials) and I know that community professionally, including Jihong Yu, who is a credited name on the ballot but not in my proposed configuration. My profile records no collaboration, mentorship or institutional tie to Corma, Davis, Zones, Yu or Tsapatsis. The chair's summary notes a Stockholm University colleague relationship with Secretary Brzezinski, which is procedural. I would step back from B018 if a closer tie were shown.
